project_specification.project_name: nullius — operator surfaces for the middle loop, the canary, the M1 triage and the gate metrics (journeys J17–J20)
project_specification.addition_summary: Journey Run 7 (docs/user-journeys/_run-log.md, 2026-10-06) re-read the PRD and the architecture and found capabilities that exist as library code but that no operator can reach: - J17: no command runs a dreaming cycle (PRD §5 Loop 2, the M3 gate), and no command fills the bootstrap pool (PRD M1.5). - J18: nothing runs or schedules the determinism canary (architecture §12), and the dashboard's canary lamp reads "ok" on a fresh install where no canary has ever run, because the lamp is only "dreaming is not halted". - J19: no command runs the M1 perturbation-stability triage. - J20: the gate-evidence metrics (sensitivity/specificity, Type-B depth, discoveries per 1000 charged trials, the train-vs-holdout gap) are persisted but neither served nor shown. - J21 (observation): bingx_heartbeat prints nothing about its verdict. - Found while checking completeness: outside the demo seeder, nothing writes FDR_deploy, the KS guard reading, the sensitivity/specificity pair, Type-B depth or the discovery rate. A real campaign closes without producing the PRD's headline number. A campaign close-out step, run by the scorer process that holds the sidecar key, fills them. This spec adds those operator surfaces. It composes existing member functions; it adds no new statistics and no new dependency outside the workspace.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite or PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions) / Streamlit dashboard / stdlib http.server API.
existing_context.test_baseline: Journey Run 7 on main at fe3f694: J1–J15 pass. The run's acceptance gate measures its own tests/ baseline; member suites under packages/*/tests are run per member.
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md. Never recreate src/app/modules/. Typed refusals open with a greppable code word. Tests never reach the network, never read a credential, and pass under pytest-xdist (no module-level mutable state, unique ids and tmp databases per test).
House CLI pattern, as in orchestrator/campaign.py and router/bingx_heartbeat.py: argparse with prog="python -m pkg.mod" built in _build_parser(); main(argv=None, *, env=None, app=None, emit=print, ...) -> int; `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`. Exit 0 = done, 1 = a collaborator refused (print str(exc) to stderr, prefixed once with the module's code word), 2 = bad argument or missing configuration. Output is one JSON line per event via emit(json.dumps(...)). A missing composed component prints one stderr line naming it, never a traceback.
Existing pieces (read them; edit only the files a feature names): - canary: CanaryReferenceStore(database_url).load(reference_id) and .freeze(pair, *, reference_id=None, stored_at=None); CanaryPolicy.freeze(version=, policy=), CanaryTree.freeze({...}), CanaryReferencePair(policy, tree, recorded_score, id, is_active, created_at); replay_pair(pair, *, tolerance=DEFAULT_TOLERANCE) -> CanaryReplayResult (score, recorded_score, deviation, within_tolerance, tolerance, .broken); halt_dreaming(pair, result, *, database_url=None, env=None, detected_at=None) writes canary_dream_halt and raises CanaryDeterminismBrokenError (determinism_broken); void_scores_after_break(...); require_dreaming_allowed(); CanaryHaltStore.halted(). Nothing records a successful run today. The fixture pair in packages/canary/tests/test_replay.py (_policy, _tree) replays to 0.66. - dreaming: CycleFreeze(url).open(iteration_id) / .release(hold); revise_policy(incumbent_source, count, *, seed, reviser=None) (the default reviser is the no-network AST jitter); include_incumbent; split_replay_pool(*, database_url, rotation, floor=20, train_fraction, env); record_cycle_holdout; revision_cap(world_count) and record_cycle_cap; rejects_thin_pool(world_count) raising PoolTooThinError (pool_too_thin, floor LADDER_FLOOR_WORLDS = 20); sweep_candidates(candidates, *, evaluator, beta, worlds=None, split=None, database_url=None) writing one replay_score row per (candidate, world); commit_selection(candidates, *, strata, beta, iteration_id=None, database_url=None) writing policy_revision. The only evaluator today is a stub in tests/e2e/test_dreaming_cycle_bootstrap_selection.py. - bootstrap: BootstrapPool(url).ensure_schema(), .persist_worlds(count=45, *, pool_seed=20260922) (count in [40, 50]), .world_count(), .worlds(), .world(world_id); world_census(pool) -> WorldCensus(n_financial, n_bootstrap, .total); question_for(world) -> BootstrapQuestion (observed, legal_roots, legal_actions, meta, probe_batch, budget_remaining, commit, committed); the world's ground truth (GroundTruth.score) labels every node exactly. - policy loading: orchestrator._policy screens a policy source with policy_runtime.screen_policy, imports it under POLICY_MODULE_NAME and runs it under policy_runtime.guard_policy. That guard is defence-in-depth, not an isolation boundary. - tripwires.triage: run_triage(*, seed=TRIAGE_SEED, count=TRIAGE_POPULATION) -> TriageFigure with .to_payload(); pure, no stores, about 15 s; refusals TripwirePanelError / TripwireStatisticError. - ops stores (each resolve(env) -> store | None, record(...), a point read, history() ordered by recorded_at): NullCalibrations ("ops-null-calibration"), TypeBDepths ("ops-type-b-depth"), DiscoveryRates ("ops-discovery-rate"), MetaOverfitGaps ("ops-meta-overfit", keyed by iteration_id). The route pattern to copy is ops/regime_coverage.py (ROUTE constant, Endpoint.from_env, no-arg get() returning a frozen dataclass, store errors translated) plus an API_ROUTES row in nullius_api/routes.py and an HTTP_ADAPTERS entry (_no_argument_get) in nullius_api/server.py. - ops/instrument_status.py builds canary = not halted and refuses a non-bool canary; ops/chrome.py already renders None as "no reading".

category.name: Determinism Canary Operation
category.feature: System runs the determinism canary from `python -m canary.run`, which records every run so that "the canary ran and passed" is a stored fact rather than the absence of a halt. - A new append-only table canary_run (id, reference_id, ran_at, score, recorded_score, deviation, tolerance, within_tolerance) is created by a CanaryRunStore(database_url) with record(...) and newest() -> CanaryRun | None, exported from canary and registered as the "canary-run-store" component (None without DATABASE_URL). - `python -m canary.run --freeze-reference` freezes the built-in reference pair (the policy and tree of the existing replay fixture, moved into run.py as module constants), with recorded_score equal to its own replay score and is_active true, and prints the reference_id. If an active pair already exists, it refuses with code word canary_reference_exists and exit 1, changing nothing. - `python -m canary.run` (no flag) loads the single active reference pair, replays it with replay_pair, records one canary_run row and prints one JSON line (reference_id, score, recorded_score, deviation, within_tolerance, ran_at), then exits 0. - On a deviation beyond the tolerance it records the row, then calls halt_dreaming (which writes canary_dream_halt) and void_scores_after_break, prints the JSON line with within_tolerance false, and exits 3. Exit 3 is reserved for a broken canary, so a systemd OnFailure hook can tell it apart from a configuration fault. - No DATABASE_URL raises exit 2 with one line. No active pair, or more than one, raises exit 1 with code word canary_reference_absent or canary_reference_ambiguous. Neither prints a traceback. - Tests cover: freeze then run gives exit 0, one row and within_tolerance true; a second freeze is refused; a tampered recorded_score gives exit 3, a halt row and a run row; an empty store gives canary_reference_absent; newest() returns the latest row. Every test passes under pytest-xdist.

System displays the canary lamp in three states, and GET /metrics/instrument-status returns 200 with canary true, false or null, so neither ever claims "replay is deterministic" for a canary that has not run. - The canary field becomes Optional[bool]: - False when CanaryHaltStore.halted() is true. A halt wins over everything, as today. - True only when the newest canary_run row (feature 1's CanaryRunStore.newest()) has within_tolerance true and ran within CANARY_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 36 of the read. - None ("no reading") when no run has been recorded or the newest one is older than that. - The response gains canary_last_run_at (ISO-8601 string or None). The chrome renders None as "no reading" with no change to ops/chrome.py, matching the KS lamp's existing absence rule. - The module docstring's "canary is never absent" rule is replaced by this rule. The tests that pinned it are rewritten to pin the three states. The api test that asserted canary is True on an empty store now asserts it is None. - A store that cannot be read is still refused (translated), never answered None or True.

category.name: Middle Loop Operation
category.feature: System saves bootstrap worlds to the pool from `python -m bootstrap.fill --count N --pool-seed S` (defaults 45 and 20260922), and displays the pool's census as one JSON line. - It calls BootstrapPool(url).ensure_schema() then persist_worlds(count, pool_seed=S), and prints one JSON line: n_bootstrap, n_financial, total and pool_seed. - Re-running with the same arguments writes nothing new and prints the same census. If the pool already holds worlds drawn from a different pool_seed, it refuses with code word bootstrap_pool_populated and exit 1, writing nothing. - `--census` prints the census without writing. A count outside [40, 50] is refused with exit 1 using the member's own BootstrapPoolError text. No DATABASE_URL gives exit 2. - Tests cover fill, idempotent re-run, the different-seed refusal, census-only on an empty store (zeros), and the bad count. Every test passes under pytest-xdist.

System scores one (candidate policy, bootstrap world) pair with orchestrator._bootstrap_eval.score_on_world(candidate_source, world, *, round_cap) and returns a carrier with .pick and .score, the shape dreaming.sweep_candidates expects of its evaluator. - It screens the source with policy_runtime.screen_policy, imports it under POLICY_MODULE_NAME and runs it under guard_policy, as orchestrator._policy does. A source that fails screening raises PolicyLoadError naming the admission reason. - It drives the candidate's select over bootstrap.question_for(world) until no batch is returned or the round cap is reached, then reads the committed node. The score is the world's own ground-truth score of that node. A policy that commits nothing returns pick None and score replay.NON_COMMITTING_SCORE. - The same source, world and round cap return the same pick and score twice (determinism). - Tests use one persisted bootstrap world in a tmp SQLite store and three tiny policy sources: one that commits the best observed node, one that never commits, and one that fails screening. They make no network call and pass under pytest-xdist.

System runs one dreaming cycle over the stored world pool from `python -m orchestrator.dream --incumbent PATH [--iteration-id ID] [--beta 0.5] [--seed S] [--round-cap 30]`. It prints the selected policy revision and its train-vs-holdout gap, so the M3 gate's inputs can be produced by an operator. - Order of checks, each before any write: 1. DATABASE_URL present, else exit 2. 2. Dreaming not halted by the canary (require_dreaming_allowed), else exit 1 with determinism_broken. 3. Pool size from world_census(pool).total checked with rejects_thin_pool, else exit 1 with pool_too_thin naming the count and the floor of 20. 4. The incumbent source screened with policy_runtime.screen_policy, else exit 1 naming the admission reason. - Then: M = revision_cap(total), recorded with record_cycle_cap. CycleFreeze.open(iteration_id); revise_policy(incumbent, M, seed=S) with the default no-network reviser, then include_incumbent; release. split_replay_pool(rotation = iteration_id) gives the 70/30 split, recorded with record_cycle_holdout. sweep_candidates over every world, then commit_selection over the train worlds only. - The sweep's evaluator is feature 4's score_on_world. - Financial worlds are not scored by this CLI. They are counted in n_financial and reported, and the summary says they were skipped. - After selection it records MetaOverfitGaps.record(iteration_id, train_mean, holdout_mean, train_worlds, holdout_worlds) for the selected candidate, and prints one JSON summary line: iteration_id, n_bootstrap, n_financial, M, the selected module_id and code_hash, train_mean, holdout_mean, gap, and the replay_score row count. - `--write-selected PATH` writes the selected candidate's source to PATH (refusing to overwrite an existing file), so the operator can point NULLIUS_EXPLORATION_POLICY at it and the next campaign explores with π_{t+1}. Without the flag nothing is written outside the store. - `--reviser llm` is refused with code word policy_isolation_required and exit 1. LLM-authored policy code must not execute in the host process until policies have an OS sandbox (CLAUDE.md, SEC-1). `--reviser jitter` (the default) derives every candidate from the operator's own incumbent. - pyproject.toml gains the workspace members the module imports (dreaming, bootstrap, canary, ops, replay) and nothing else, and uv.lock is regenerated with `uv lock` to match. - Tests run against a tmp SQLite store filled with BootstrapPool.persist_worlds(40, ...) and a small incumbent policy source: - one cycle exits 0, writes one replay_score row per (candidate, world), writes one selected policy_revision and one meta-overfit row - a rerun with the same iteration_id and seed selects the same code_hash - an empty pool exits 1 with pool_too_thin and writes nothing - a recorded canary halt exits 1 with determinism_broken - --reviser llm exits 1 with policy_isolation_required - an incumbent that fails screening exits 1 The tests make no network call and pass under pytest-xdist.

System runs the M1 triage experiment from `python -m tripwires.triage [--seed S] [--count N]` and displays the perturbation-stability AUC with the reading PRD §12 M1 assigns to it, or an error message with exit 1. - It calls run_triage(seed=S, count=N) and prints one JSON line: the payload of to_payload() plus a reading field derived only from the mean AUC: - "robustness_filter_suffices" when the AUC is 0.80 or more - "learned_signature_warranted" when it is 0.65 or less - "indeterminate" otherwise The thresholds are module constants, and the line names the population as the member's planted panel. - A bad seed or a count below 2 gives exit 1, printing the member's TripwirePanelError text, with no traceback. The run itself reads no store and makes no network call. - Tests use a small --count, so they run in seconds. They assert the JSON keys, the reading for a stubbed figure on each side of each threshold, and the refusal. They pass under pytest-xdist.

category.name: Gate Evidence Surfaces
category.feature: System serves the M3 gate evidence through four read endpoints in a new ops/gate_evidence.py, following the ops/regime_coverage.py pattern. - The routes are /metrics/null-calibration, /metrics/type-b-depth, /metrics/discovery-rate and /metrics/meta-overfit, registered as the components "ops-null-calibration-route", "ops-type-b-depth-route", "ops-discovery-rate-route" and "ops-meta-overfit-route". Each is None without DATABASE_URL. - Each get() returns a frozen dataclass holding the store's history() (oldest first) and its newest row. An empty store answers an empty history and newest None, never a zero. Store errors are translated to the module's own error class. - The route constants are exported from ops. No is_null label or per-node null status appears in any response: these stores hold only aggregates. - Tests cover empty and populated stores for all four, and an unreadable store giving the translated error.

System exposes feature 6's four endpoints over HTTP under the metrics:read scope. GET /metrics/null-calibration, /metrics/type-b-depth, /metrics/discovery-rate and /metrics/meta-overfit each answer 200 with the JSON body, 401 without a token, 403 with a token of another scope, and 503 component_unconfigured when the component is None. - Four API_ROUTES rows and four HTTP_ADAPTERS entries (_no_argument_get). The index reads "14 routes declared". The pinned route lists and counts in test_routes.py and test_discoverability.py are updated to 14. - test_metrics_routes.py gains a test that drives each new route through the real server on port 0 over a populated tmp store, and checks every body is encoded by json_encoding with no traceback.

System shows a "Gate evidence" section on the operator dashboard below the FDR_deploy panel and its trend chart. It never sits above or beside the headline, so FDR_deploy stays the one top-line figure (architecture §16). - The section is one subheader and four captions: - "sensitivity / specificity" for the newest campaign - "Type-B depth past flip" - "discoveries per 1000 charged trials" - "train-vs-holdout gap" for the newest dreaming iteration Each caption names the campaign or iteration it belongs to. A store with no row renders "no reading", never 0. - DashboardPage gains an optional evidence seat, read in page() after the existing reads. A dashboard composed without the four components renders the section as "no reading" lines rather than failing. The existing primary panel, lamps and epoch chrome are unchanged. - No profit, P&L or equity figure appears in the section. - test_dashboard.py's RENDER_SEQUENCE transcript is extended with the section. Tests cover populated, empty and unconfigured evidence.

category.name: Campaign Close-out
category.feature: System closes out a finished campaign from `python -m orchestrator.closeout --campaign-id ID`. It saves the campaign's calibration figures to the stores the dashboard and API read, and displays them as one JSON line, so FDR_deploy is measured for real campaigns and not only for the demo seeder. - The command is the scorer process: it builds scoring.NullPickScorer.resolve(env) from NULL_SIDECAR_PATH and NULL_SIDECAR_KEY_REF. Without a sidecar, or without DATABASE_URL, it exits 2 naming the missing variable. - It reads the campaign's evaluated node rows. A discovery is an evaluated node (fail_class ok) whose ic_tstat is at least DISCOVERY_TSTAT = 2.0, a documented module constant (the in-sample bar at roughly p < 0.05). - In order: 1. nulloracle.KsGuard.guard over the in-sample ic_mean of the campaign's null nodes vs its real nodes. The split happens inside the scorer process; only the two score lists reach the guard. 2. The campaign verdict (nulloracle's build_verdict component, feature 124), which marks the campaign VOID when p < 0.05. 3. NullPickScorer.calibration_figures(population = the campaign's planted nodes, picks = its discoveries). 4. scoring.FdrDeployStore.persist(campaign_id, figures). 5. ops NullCalibrations.record. 6. For a Type-D campaign only, scoring.account_errors gives the Type-B depth past the flip, saved with ops TypeBDepths.record. 7. ops DiscoveryRates.record, with the ledger's budget-charging and total trial counts for the campaign. - The JSON line carries campaign_id, ks_pvalue, calibration_status, sensitivity, specificity, fdr_deploy, type_b (or null for Type-R), discoveries, budget_charging_trials and ledger_trials. It never carries a node id together with a null label (PRD §4.2). - Exit 0 when the campaign is calibrated. Exit 3 when the verdict is VOID: the figures are still saved, and the exit code lets an alert hook fire. Exit 1 when a collaborator refuses (an unknown campaign, or a one-sided plant), with its error message and no traceback. - Running it twice on one campaign saves no duplicate rows and prints the same line. - Tests use a tmp store and a tmp sidecar built the way nullius_api.demo builds one, over a small Type-R campaign and a small Type-D campaign. They assert the saved rows in all five stores, the VOID path (exit 3), idempotence, and that no stdout line pairs a node id with null status. They make no network call and pass under pytest-xdist.

System closes out every campaign the campaign CLI finishes. After the summary line, `python -m orchestrator.campaign` runs feature 13's close-out on the finished campaign_id and displays its JSON line. - A close-out refusal is printed as one stderr line and makes the command exit 1. The campaign itself stays recorded, and the operator can rerun `python -m orchestrator.closeout` once the cause is fixed. - A VOID verdict makes the campaign CLI exit 3. - `--no-closeout` skips the step for a deployment without a sidecar, and says so on stderr. - test_campaign_cli.py gains tests for the close-out line, the refusal path and --no-closeout, with collaborators stubbed as the existing tests stub them.

category.name: Operator Wiring and Hygiene
category.feature: System prints the heartbeat's verdict. `python -m router.bingx_heartbeat` writes one JSON line to stdout, with verdict "fresh", "stale" or "absent", newest_slot (or null), age_hours (or null) and max_age_hours. It does this whether or not the alert could be delivered, so an operator running it by hand learns the bot's state even without Telegram configured. - Exit codes, alert deduplication and the logged delivery faults are unchanged. - The tests that pinned an empty stdout now pin the one verdict line for fresh, stale and absent.

System wires the new commands into run.sh and systemd, so `./run.sh help` displays the five new verbs. - run.sh gains `closeout` (python -m orchestrator.closeout "$@"), run under `op run --env-file=.env.campaign.tpl` exactly like the campaign verb, because it needs the sidecar key reference. It also gains four verbs that never use op run, because none needs a secret: - `canary` (python -m canary.run "$@") - `bootstrap-fill` (python -m bootstrap.fill "$@") - `dream` (python -m orchestrator.dream "$@") - `triage` (python -m tripwires.triage "$@") Each defaults DATABASE_URL to sqlite:///$HOME/.local/share/nullius/research.db, as the campaign verb does, and is listed by `./run.sh help`. - deploy/systemd gains nullius-canary.service (oneshot, `run.sh canary`, OnFailure=nullius-vst-alert@%n.service) and nullius-canary.timer (daily at 03:15 UTC, Persistent=true). They mirror the existing VST units' form, and nothing installs or enables them.

System documents the new commands where operators look for them, so the README displays a canary that actually runs. - README.md's "Running" section and CLAUDE.md's orchestrator section gain the five verbs (canary, bootstrap-fill, dream, triage, closeout) and the canary timer, each with its exit codes, and say that a campaign now closes itself out, so FDR_deploy is measured for real campaigns. - J19's step 2 expectation is corrected to say what the triage measures: the member's planted panel, with no sidecar read.

project_specification.integration_points: Features 1–3, 5, 6 and 9 are independent. Feature 2 reads feature 1's CanaryRunStore. Feature 4 (the evaluator) depends on feature 3; feature 11 (the dreaming CLI) depends on features 1, 3 and 4. Features 7 and 8 read feature 6's endpoints. Feature 14 depends on feature 13. Feature 10 alone edits run.sh and deploy/, and feature 12 alone edits the docs, so no two features contend for those files.
project_specification.out_of_scope: Running LLM-authored exploration policies in the dreaming cycle (blocked on a policy OS sandbox). Scoring financial worlds inside the dreaming CLI. The live metrics (live-vs-backtest IC ratio, fill cost, reject rate), deferred to M4/M5 by the owner's recorded J20 decision. The full operator console of docs/design.md.
